papers.title: A structure-based model of the bacterial chemosensory array reveals how the scaffolding protein CheW tunes sensory responses
papers.abstract: We introduce a structure-based Ising model of the bacterial chemosensory array to investigate how the scaffolding protein CheW tunes signaling responses. The model couples the activity states of core signaling units and of CheW subunits within hexameric rings on a lattice with the structure observed in cryoEM experiments. Recent experiments show that increasing CheW participation in hexameric rings raises response cooperativity in non-adapting cells and sensitivity in adaptation-proficient cells. Our lattice model quantitatively reproduces both effects, while mean-field theory shows that CheW increases the effective coupling between core units, sharpening the response in both cell types. The statistics of CheW placement (complete hexameric rings versus random distribution) substantially alter how responses vary with CheW abundance. Moreover, different coupling strengths can yield the same static response yet markedly different activity fluctuations and dynamics. CheW abundance further controls a crossover from relaxational to oscillatory fluctuations, whose location depends on the spatial distribution of CheW. These dynamical signatures, including oscillations predicted near native CheW levels, are testable by single-cell dynamics measurements. Combined with CheW titration and our modeling results, these measurements can probe the array's assembly dynamics and allosteric couplings. Beyond the chemosensory array, our approach can generalize to other large protein complexes, providing a framework to study the functional role of scaffolding proteins and allosteric interfaces in signal processing.

papers.title: Semi-Implicit and Convex Splitting Schemes for the Surface Cahn--Hilliard Equation on Curved Closed Surfaces
papers.abstract: The surface Cahn--Hilliard equation describes phase separation and coarsening of a conserved composition field on fixed curved surfaces. We study a mixed $hp$-surface finite element discretization with curvilinear high-order elements, primarily on the sphere, with the stabilized semi-implicit BDF2 integrator and a stabilized convex-splitting variant solved with the same factorization. For the semi-implicit scheme with a quadratic-growth potential and a truncated nonlinear bulk chemical-potential term, we prove exact discrete mass conservation, energy decay for the start-up steps, an exact per-step energy balance for the BDF2 phase, and a conditional monotone law for a modified Lyapunov functional. A manufactured solution with analytic forcing verifies second order in time and the expected $h$- and $p$-convergence. Torus tests include controlled equal-area bands, whose diffuse energies reproduce sharp-interface perimeters within $1\%$, deterministic coarsening, and a viscous R{ä}tz--Voigt model. Genus-two and genus-three calculations on implicit surfaces conserve mass to roundoff, and their unstable-mode counts agree with area-based Weyl estimates within $1\%$.

papers.title: Time-Decay Rates toward a Rarefaction-Contact-Shock Composite Wave for the One-Dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier Equations
papers.abstract: We consider the one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes-Fourier equations when the end states are connected by a rarefaction wave, a contact discontinuity, and a shock. For a fixed weak nonzero shock, sufficiently weak rarefaction and contact waves, and small H^2(R) initial perturbations, we establish asymptotic stability with a time-dependent shift on the viscous shock. The L^4 time average of the uniform perturbation and the shift velocity over [t,2t] is bounded by C_S(1+t)^(-1/4). We prove pointwise-in-time bounds of order (1+t)^(-1/12) on the whole line, (1+t)^(-1/4) near the shifted shock, and (1+t)^(-1/6) on |x| >= \eta t for each fixed \eta>0. The proof uses energy estimates and comparison on finite time interval

papers.title: MIMO Channel Extrapolation to Unobserved Radiation Modes via Learned Path Refinement
papers.abstract: A pattern-reconfigurable multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) receiver can sample every antenna element and still leave entire radiation modes unobserved. The calibrated patterns weight a common set of propagation paths, which links these missing channels to the measured rows. Our estimator learns to correct the complex gains and spatial frequencies of those paths, so a correction inferred from measured rows updates every unmeasured mode. Each stage combines a damped least-squares proposal with a learned correction scaled by noise power and local array sensitivity. Training on complete simulated channels rewards corrections that reduce prediction error across modes, including those with no measured rows. The learned rule transfers from pursuit-based training estimates to a ridge variable-projection initializer without retraining. In matched simulations, refinement reduces error on wholly unobserved modes as well as across the full channel. Coefficient updates account for most of the gain, and the learned rule further improves on adaptive ridge shrinkage at fixed angles. Individual channel trajectories show that extrapolation can improve even as the residual on the measured rows increases.

papers.title: Constructive Trend to Equilibrium for Low-regularity Boltzmann and BGK equations
papers.abstract: We study the long-time behavior of global mild solutions to the cutoff Boltzmann and BGK equations on $\T^3$ under a Gaussian lower bound and a polynomially weighted $L^\infty$ upper bound. The main step is a finite-time estimate which uses free transport to control the entropy of the local Maxwellian by microscopic entropy and dissipation, without assuming Sobolev regularity. For Boltzmann, Villani's entropy-production inequality and a comparison of collision kernels give polynomial decay when the velocity weight has order $m>7$. For a sufficiently large weight, the large-amplitude theory then gives exponential decay in the weighted norm and in relative entropy. For BGK, the microscopic inequality is linear, so entropy decays exponentially from the finite-time estimate. Finally, we establish a density criterion for large-data BGK dynamics in the polynomially weighted $L^\infty$ class of Perthame and Pulvirenti. For weight order $m>10$, a uniform upper bound on the local density guarantees uniform-in-time weighted bounds and exponential convergence to equilibrium in both relative entropy and the weighted $L^\infty$ norm.

papers.title: On global error estimates of a local discontinuous Galerkin method of the Boussinesq system of equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop and analyze a local discontinuous Galerkin (LDG) finite element method for the Boussinesq system of equations, and employ an upwind scheme to effectively manage the nonlinear convective terms, thereby ensuring stability and accuracy. Our analysis establishes new \emph{a priori} regularity estimates for the semidiscrete LDG approximations. We establish optimal \emph{a priori} error estimates for the velocity approximation in $\bL^2$--norm, the pressure approximation in $L^2$--norm and for temperature in $L^2$--norm for all $t>0$. Our proof relies on the standard elliptic and parabolic duality arguments and modified Stokes operators defined on appropriate broken Sobolev spaces. Under suitable smallness assumptions on the given data, we further establish error estimates that remain uniform in time. Furthermore, the backward Euler scheme is considered for a full discretization, and optimal fully discrete error estimates are derived. Finally, we carry out numerical experiments to substantiate our theoretical findings.

papers.title: Categorified Koszul duality and deformation theory of higher categories
papers.abstract: This paper develops a deformation theory for stable $(\infty,n)$-categories for $n > 1$. We introduce the framework of complete $t$-structured stable presentable $(\infty,n)$-categories. Within this setting, we establish a higher categorified Koszul duality among complete $t$-structured presentable $(\infty,n)$-categories. Using this duality, we develop the deformation theory. We prove that the deformation problem for such categories is a well-behaved formal moduli problem determined by Hochschild cohomology, and we deduce the corresponding obstruction theory. Finally, we apply our results to sheaves of categories on perfect stacks.

papers.title: Projected Sensitivity of a Differential Torsion Sensor for Tests of the Weak Equivalence Principle
papers.abstract: Tests of the weak equivalence principle (WEP) are among the most sensitive probes of new long-range, composition-dependent interactions beyond general relativity and the Standard Model. We evaluate the potential of a differential torsion sensor, which combines long mechanical coherence times with optical-cavity readout and common-mode rejection, for laboratory WEP tests and fifth-force searches. For a representative configuration based on an existing prototype, with Be-Ti test masses and 180 days of coherent integration, the projected noise-limited sensitivity to the Eötvös parameter is $\eta\simeq7.5\times10^{-16}$ and $2.4\times10^{-16}$ for signal modulation at 2 and 20 mHz, respectively, below current ground-based torsion-balance limits. For a baryon-coupled Yukawa interaction sourced by the Earth, the corresponding projected sensitivity to the coupling strength is $\alpha\simeq3.1\times10^{-13}$ and $9.8\times10^{-14}$ for ranges $\lambda\gtrsim10^{7}$ m. We identify the modulation scheme, the material contrast, and the source geometry as the main factors that set the projected reach, and the control of systematic couplings as the main experimental requirement for attaining it. These results indicate that differential torsion sensors are a promising platform for future laboratory WEP tests.

papers.title: DIVO: a direct divertor configuration plasma start-up scheme aimed at tokamak fusion reactors
authors: Hailing Zhao (1) ((1) Institute of Plasma Physics
United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
papers.abstract: The tokamak, one of the mainstream approaches to magnetic confinement in nuclear fusion devices, will be the first approach to reach reactor class prototyping. Plasma start-up is expected to be more challenging in large superconducting next-step tokamaks such as ITER due to the low inductive toroidal electric field and potentially long durations in limiter configuration when plasma-wall interactions lead to easier impurity contamination of the confined plasma. Such limiter start-up is the standard way of early plasma formation in the vast majority of today's experimental devices and is planned on ITER. To mitigate these issues, a novel plasma start-up scheme with divertor geometry only (DIVO start-up) was recently developed for the first time on the EAST superconducting tokamak. The key breakthrough in this work is the use of a non-inductive, electron cyclotron wave generated plasma formed in a poloidal field configuration which is a superposition of a barrel-like geometry around the centre of the vacuum vessel and a mirror-like geometry across the whole vessel cross-section. Such a non-inductive discharge avoids the drawback of low inductive electric field which is unavoidable in large superconducting devices as a consequence of the relatively low voltages which can be applied to the magnet coils. In addition to the low toroidal electric field, the DIVO start-up scheme as demonstrated on EAST significantly reduces impurity sources compared to the conventional limiter phase approach, even in cases with relatively poorly conditioned plasma-facing surfaces. The robustness of the DIVO start-up has also been verified on EAST with varying prefill gas pressure, impurity level and inductive electric field. It thus offers a potential solution to one of the main issues facing routine successful start-up on large tokamak reactors.

papers.title: Asymptotic error of the accelerated exponential Euler scheme for semilinear parabolic SPDEs driven by fractional Brownian motion
papers.abstract: We study the strong convergence and asymptotic error of the accelerated exponential Euler scheme for semilinear parabolic stochastic partial differential equations driven by additive cylindrical fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H\in(\frac12,1)$. The drift is globally Lipschitz and Gâteaux differentiable, with a second directional derivative taking values in a negative-order space. Under a weighted Hilbert--Schmidt condition on the noise and suitable derivative bounds, we establish strong error estimates that reflect the interaction between noise regularity and drift regularity. In a regime where the strong order is one, the normalized error $m(X^m-X)$ converges in probability in $C([0,T];\V)$ to the unique continuous solution of a random linear integral equation. Its stochastic forcing is a divergence integral plus an explicit covariance correction. The proof combines a Gâteaux chain rule for Malliavin derivatives, uniform spectral approximations, and time increment estimates. Localization gives the result for independent random initial values with finite moments, together with lower-moment convergence at each fixed time.

papers.title: Vague rotational symmetry at BCC [100] twist grain boundaries
papers.abstract: In earlier work ( arXiv:2603.21158 ) we introduced vague rotational symmetry for proximal coincidence point sets at grain boundaries. A prescribed rotation must be realizable at every pair tolerance $\varepsilon$ by moving each midpoint of an admitted atomic pair by at most $\varepsilon/2$, half the maximum pair separation. We prove the proposed classification for the planar model of a body-centred cubic $[100]$ twist boundary. On $0\leq\theta\leq45^\circ$, the maximal rotational order is twelve at $30^\circ$, eight at $45^\circ$, and four at every other misorientation. Vague $n$-fold symmetry forces $\xi_n M=M$ for the Fourier module $M$, hence $\mathbb{Z}[\xi_n]\subseteq M$ in crystal coordinates. For every rotation of finite order preserving $M$, we determine the least uniform displacement for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, allowing independent point motions and a free rotation centre. In this regime twelvefold symmetry at $30^\circ$ costs $\varepsilon/(2\sqrt3)$, and eightfold symmetry at $45^\circ$ costs zero. At a twist of approximately $25.53^\circ$, the Fourier module also has eightfold symmetry, but realizing it in the plane costs $\sqrt2\,\varepsilon$.

papers.title: Imaging chiral snake states in a qubit array with programmable gauge fields
papers.abstract: Spatially varying magnetic fields steer charged particles along directed paths. Where a field reverses sign, particles follow snake-like orbits along the reversal line, in a direction set by both the field orientation and the sign of their energy. Transport measurements have detected such snake states, but imaging their dynamics in a reprogrammable field landscape remains challenging. Here we digitally simulate the Harper--Hofstadter model with programmable synthetic magnetic fields on a 49-qubit superconducting processor. In each Trotter step, every hopping term is one native fractional-iSWAP gate, and single-qubit $Z$ rotations set all 36 plaquette fluxes independently, without additional entangling gates. Uniform, random, and stepped flux landscapes reveal Aharonov--Bohm suppression of diagonal propagation, disorder-induced slowing, and magnetic reflection. At a field reversal, bonding and antibonding initial states, which carry opposite energy biases, propagate in opposite directions, and both directions reverse when the field is inverted. A symmetry analysis of these reversals yields a chiral displacement of nearly one lattice spacing after ten Trotter rounds, with symmetry-breaking residuals below 0.05 lattice spacings. Bond-resolved flux programming with site-resolved imaging thus provides a quantitative tool for synthetic gauge fields and a route to time-dependent gauge fields and interacting particles.

papers.title: Quasi-Bisections of Cubic Graphs with Tree and Circuit Decompositions
papers.abstract: A $2$-quasi-bisection of a graph is a vertex $2$-coloring in which the color classes differ in size by at most two and every monochromatic component has at most two vertices. Esperet, Mazzuoccolo, and Tarsi in [J. Graph Theory, 86(2017), 149-158] conjectured that every cubic graph admits such a coloring. DeVos and Nurse proved the conjecture for cubic graphs whose edge sets can be partitioned into a tree and a circuit. This result is generalized in this paper for a larger family of cubic graphs. The conjecture is verified for cubic graphs whose edge set can be partitioned into two subsets $E(T)$ and $E(J)$, where $T$ is a tree of $G$ and $J$ is an even subgraph containing at most two odd circuit components.

papers.title: Long-lived linear slow roll near critical and spinodal points in soft-wall AdS/QCD
papers.abstract: We systematically investigate the real-time evolution of the chiral condensate near critical and spinodal points within soft-wall AdS/QCD, focusing primarily on the long-lived prethermalization stage, in contrast to the conventional early transients and late-time relaxation. While the quasi-steady nature of this stage has been previously identified, we demonstrate that it is intrinsically a continuous linear slow roll, fundamentally distinct from the asymptotic critical slowing down at late times. By showing that the bulk evolution adiabatically follows the boundary condensate on a slow configuration space, we analytically project the 5D partial differential equation onto a boundary first-order Ginzburg-Landau (GL) equation. We find that the long lifetime of this linear regime is protected by a ``double-zero'' condition: the simultaneous vanishing of the local potential gradient (suppressing the drift velocity) and curvature (suppressing the acceleration). This geometric flatness inherently emerges at the second-order point and both first-order spinodal endpoints. Crucially, this behavior is not a fine-tuned artifact, but a generic consequence of the effective potential landscape intrinsic to these phase-transition endpoints, persisting across a broad class of physically relevant initial conditions and temperature quenches. A local short-time expansion further relates the interval duration to the potential curvature and its higher-order derivatives, in good agreement with our numerical simulations. This work establishes a direct link between the local structure of phase-transition endpoints and the dynamical evolution of the long-lived intermediate stage of the condensate.

papers.title: Local spin constraints and symmetry in single-$Q$ spiral magnets
papers.abstract: The Luttinger--Tisza (LT) method provides a lower bound on the energy of classical spin models but relaxes the local spin-length constraints. For a generic incommensurate single-$Q$ spiral, fixed spin length requires circular polarization on every magnetic sublattice, a condition not guaranteed by equal sublattice weights in the lowest LT eigenmode. We develop a constrained formulation for general bilinear classical spin Hamiltonians with one or two magnetic sublattices. For one sublattice, minimization reduces to a secular equation for the spiral-plane normal. For two sublattices, exact elimination of the relative phase gives a frame-independent energy on the space of two unit normals. We derive symmetry constraints by distinguishing operations that preserve or reverse the Fourier arm and those that preserve or exchange sublattices. For a model with symmetric anisotropy, numerical optimization over both spiral-plane normals yields a lower energy than either constrained pure exchange-sector state, despite the block diagonalization of the linear Hamiltonian. A separate anisotropic two-sublattice benchmark demonstrates that enforcing local circularity can shift the preferred ordering wave vector even when the lowest LT eigenmode has equal sublattice weights.

papers.title: Infinity-Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Principal Component Analysis: Exact Reformulation, Finite-Sample Guarantee, and Efficient Algorithm
papers.abstract: Principal component analysis (PCA) is a fundamental and ubiquitous technique for dimension reduction and representation learning, yet its empirical formulation remains vulnerable to distributional uncertainty. While distributionally robust optimization (DRO) offers a natural remedy, existing order-2 Wasserstein models of PCA either preserve the nominal PCA subspace or lack an exact reformulation. This paper demonstrates how the infinity-Wasserstein distance can reconcile these two desirable properties. For the resulting DRO model of PCA, we derive an exact finite-dimensional reformulation and explicitly identify a worst-case distribution attaining the inner maximum. Crucially, the reformulated objective retains samplewise residual information beyond the empirical covariance matrix, revealing a mechanism through which distributional robustness can reshape the learned principal subspace. Under the mild assumption that the true distribution has a finite fourth moment, we further establish a uniform finite-sample performance guarantee for the proposed model. An iteratively reweighted majorization-minimization algorithm is also developed to solve the resulting nonconvex and nonsmooth optimization problem, with a rigorous analysis of its convergence properties. Numerical experiments substantiate the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithm and the practical effectiveness of the infinity-Wasserstein model in downstream applications.

papers.title: In Situ Training of Optical Neural Networks by Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Optical neural networks promise fast, energy-efficient computing, but every device departs from its design and must be trained with the hardware. In situ training relies on an expert-built calibrated digital model of each device or on gradient-free trial and error. Coding agents, large language models that write and run programs, have shown an emergent ability to understand and edit the weights of digital neural networks. Here we introduce optics as code, a method in which a coding agent trains an optical neural network from measurements alone, through a harness that returns camera images of its probes and requires a hypothesis per request. We discovered that the agent forms a physical understanding of the optics and reparametrizes the network with interpretable optical elements tuned on the hardware. It outperforms gradient-free methods in classification and image encoding, approaching backpropagation through a calibrated model at a fraction of the cost. Needing neither per-device calibration nor gradients through the hardware, and improving with more capable models, optics as code offers a practical route to large, scalable optical neural networks and a general tool for calibrating and optimizing optical experiments.

papers.title: Indecomposable representations of $C^{\infty}(S^1,\aff)$ on polynomial spaces over jet spaces
papers.abstract: We study a class of finite dimensional complex vector spaces \(\pn\), \(n \in \bn\), consisting of polynomials on \(\jnmc\), the space of \((n-1)\) jets at a fixed point \(t_0 \in S^1\) of \(C^\infty\) functions \(S^1 \to \bc\). The loop group \(C^\infty(S^1,\aff)\) of the affine group \(\aff\) acts naturally on \(\pn\) by an indecomposable linear representation. The space \(\pn\) is canonically isomorphic to the space of holomorphic sections of a certain line bundle over the loop space of the Riemann sphere. It has an intricate structure, leading to infinite families of combinatorial identities. In this paper, we establish necessary conditions for a polynomial on \(\jnmc\) to belong to \(\pn\). Furthermore, we give partial answers to several conjectures concerning \(\pn\).

papers.title: Technical Note on Matlantis PFP v9: Extending the Element and Domain Coverage of the r2SCAN Training Data
papers.abstract: Universal machine learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) make atomistic simulations possible at scales beyond the reach of density functional theory (DFT). Matlantis PFP is a uMLIP that treats a variety of domains, including crystals, molecules, and surfaces, with a single model. PFP v8 incorporated a training dataset computed with the r2SCAN functional, chosen for its good agreement with experiment, but the elements and domains covered by that dataset were limited. Here we present Matlantis PFP v9, in which the training data computed with the r2SCAN functional are extended to the lanthanides from Pr to Lu and to the elements from Po to Cm, for a total of 96 elements, and to additional domains such as clusters and adsorption structures. The formation energies of crystals containing the newly supported elements reproduce experimental standard enthalpies of formation with the same level of accuracy as crystals composed only of previously supported elements, and the adsorption energies of molecules on transition-metal surfaces have an overall error against experiment comparable to that of DFT-PBE, although chemisorbed species are overbound. On the same type of GPU (A100), the inference speed and the maximum system size exceed those of SevenNet-Omni, a public uMLIP trained on r2SCAN data: forces are evaluated three to four times faster, and five to ten times as many atoms can be handled. As a result, PFP-R2SCAN is now applicable to systems containing rare-earth and actinide elements and to adsorption on surfaces.

papers.title: Localized active phase in the coevolving voter model with fixed links
papers.abstract: The coevolving voter model (CVM) describes the evolution of node states and network topology through copying and rewiring dynamics. It traditionally assumes that all ties can be rewired, overlooking unbreakable real-world relationships like family or close friendships. To address this, we introduce fixed links that cannot be rewired and study how these structural constraints modify the collective dynamics of the CVM. In addition to the active and frozen phases of the CVM, we find a new localized active phase in which activity is sustained, beyond a percolation transition, by a giant component of fixed links. The existence of this new phase is predicted by a moment-closure approximation that goes beyond the standard pair approximation. The finite-size manifestation of this phase is an asymmetric fragmented phase. In addition, the active-frozen transition of the CVM, manifested as a fragmentation transition for finite systems, is delayed by the existence of fixed links to larger values of the rewiring rate.

papers.title: Coupled-channel pole structure and bare-state mixing of bottom-strange heavy-quark spin partners
papers.abstract: Motivated by the observation of the $B_{s0}^*(5700)$ and the heavy-quark symmetry relations connecting the $DK$, $D^*K$, $\bar{B}K$, and $\bar B^*K$ systems, we investigate whether the same chiral dynamics can generate negative-parity partners dominated by the $\bar B_1K$ and $\bar B_2^*K$ components. We further examine how nearby bare bottom-strange states reshape the pole spectrum through coupled-channel mixing. Both the relevant $S$-wave scattering and the lower-lying $P$-wave decay channels are explicitly included in the coupled-channel calculation. In the absence of bare states, the interaction generates two negative-parity poles near $6.15$ GeV. Coupling the hadronic channels to the corresponding quark-model configurations leads to a richer two-pole structure in each sector, with the pole masses, widths, and channel residues governed by the interplay between the bare states and the hadronic dynamics. In particular, the inclusion of the bare states substantially increases the widths of the negative-parity poles with the larger $S$-wave molecular components. The resulting correlated patterns in the pole spectrum provide testable signatures for future studies of excited bottom-strange mesons.

papers.title: Generalizing the Gaster--Loustau Theorem via Generalized Discrete Markov Spectra
papers.abstract: We realize generalized Markov numbers (GM numbers) for arbitrary $k_1,k_2,k_3\in \mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ as $\lambda$-lengths of return arcs on a hyperbolic orbifold constructed from local monodromy matrices. The McShane identity of Tan--Wong--Zhang on this orbifold yields a summation identity with multiplicities for the gaps between the associated Markov--Lagrange constants and their limiting value, together with a summation inequality that counts each distinct value once. These results extend the summation identity and inequality of Gaster and Loustau to generalized Markov numbers.

papers.title: Control-Aware Separating Hyperplanes for Control Barrier Functions in Planar Navigation
papers.abstract: Separating hyperplanes are widely used in Control Barrier Function (CBF)-based collision avoidance, yet their orientations strongly govern control intervention-the deviation of the applied control from the robot's nominal command. Existing methods typically select hyperplane orientations from geometry alone. Jointly optimizing orientations and control yields a continuous, non-convex problem in which local nonlinear solvers suffer from initialization sensitivity, local minima, and unpredictable latency, while discretized orientation grids scale exponentially with obstacle count. For planar navigation of a polygonal robot among polygonal obstacles, we present a solver-free, control-aware separating hyperplane selection method that directly computes a global optimum of this joint problem at each step whenever it is feasible. Exploiting the geometry of Minkowski difference polygons, we reduce this continuous non-convex optimization to evaluating a polynomial-size set of candidate control interventions via closed-form algebraic checks, selecting the feasible candidate of minimum norm. Across 250 simulated navigation scenarios, our method reduces cumulative intervention cost by 3.6% at the median and 27.3% at the 90th percentile compared to a local nonlinear solver, and completion time by 0.6% and 5.6%, respectively. In scalability benchmarks, it achieves a 6.1x per-step speedup at 16 simultaneous obstacles.

papers.title: Tuning spreading transport in GaN HEMTs with an AlN space layer under non-equilibrium heating
papers.abstract: Lateral spreading transport dominates near-junction heat dissipation in GaN high-electron-mobility transistors, yet thermal control has largely overlooked this geometry. It neither reaches the core AlGaN/GaN region nor, beyond the spatial spreading itself, accounts for the spectral non-equilibrium of the heat source. Here we tune the spreading resistance directly by inserting a thin, highly conducting AlN space layer above the source to intercept heat and divert it laterally. We test this approach across GaN, AlGaN/GaN, and AlGaN/AlN/GaN structures under both equilibrium and longitudinal-optical (LO)-pumped non-equilibrium heating, pairing non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (NEMD) with full-band phonon Monte Carlo (MC). In equilibrium, the AlN layer lowers the spreading resistance by 38% relative to the AlGaN-capped structure and by 17% relative to bare GaN, with little change in the one-dimensional resistance. The equilibrium color map over AlN thickness and interfacial bonding shows a strong interface effect but a weak thickness trend that reverses, so the gain is set by interface admission rather than solely by thickness or bulk conductivity. This ordering is independently confirmed by gray MC simulations. Under LO pumping, the spreading resistance rises by 58-83% in NEMD and by 9-20% in MC, and the equilibrium spatial optimum weakens or even reverses. This is because an optical-to-acoustic conversion gate now precedes every spatial gate and locks energy in slow optical modes. The three gates in series (optical-to-acoustic conversion, interface admission, and lateral diversion) close into a single non-equilibrium resistance network that predicts the full-band MC cases and frames the AlN space layer as a design variable within the non-equilibrium source state.

papers.title: Comparing Data-Driven and Numerical Weather Prediction Forecasts of Extreme Weather: A Review
papers.abstract: Data-driven weather forecasting models, chiefly trained on reanalysis data, now match or beat physics-based numerical weather prediction (NWP) models on most headline scores, but whether this advantage extends to extreme weather is contested. We review peer-reviewed studies that directly compare data-driven forecasts with NWP for extremes, from nowcasting to subseasonal lead times. We discuss grey literature in the outlook but do not include it in the formal review. There is good agreement on the fact that data-driven models mostly outperform NWP on temperature extremes, tropical cyclone tracks and the location of synoptic features across time scales. The evidence is mixed for extreme precipitation and feature-based extreme event detection such as extremes related to atmospheric rivers, while it leans toward better NWP performance for estimating event intensity. For record-breaking events that lie outside the training distribution, the evidence is narrower. Nonetheless, both a systematic global evaluation and several case studies find that physics-based models retain the advantage, with data-driven models underestimating both the frequency and the magnitude of records. Hybrid systems that post-process NWP with machine-learning (ML), or couple data-driven forecasts with physics-based models, deliver some of the largest and most consistent gains. We argue that headline scores, verification choices and case selection explain much of the apparent disagreement in the literature, and provide recommendations for a more trustworthy and interpretable evaluation of data-driven models for extreme and record-breaking weather.

papers.title: Aharonov-Bohm blockade of complete reversal in coupled Rabi cavities
papers.abstract: When a common bias reverses two bistable fields, the system can pass through either of two single-reversal configurations on its way to the favored state. We show that interference between these two orders of reversal can block the final step. In a dimer of coupled quantum Rabi cavities, the four field configurations form a loop, and a complex photon-hopping amplitude threads it with an Aharonov-Bohm flux. Near half a flux quantum, the two paths to complete reversal interfere destructively: in microscopic simulations, a slow uniform sweep reverses one field with probability 0.998, although the final bias favors reversing both. A four-state model calibrated at zero bias predicts how the window of this Aharonov-Bohm blockade narrows with sweep time. The blocked state remains coherent. A differential pulse followed by a return sweep converts the relative phase of the two single-reversal configurations into a fringe in the joint field signs, with contrast 0.95. In a trimer, a phase gradient imprinted between sweeps determines whether the next sweep adds or removes a reversed field: reversing the second of two gradients changes the most probable outcome from three reversed fields to one.

papers.title: Graded version of local-global principle for Steinberg and Chevalley groups
papers.abstract: In this article, an analog of a graded version of Quillen-Suslin's local-global principle was established for Steinberg groups $St(\Phi,-)$ and Chevalley groups $G(\Phi,-)$ over a reduced irreducible root system $\Phi$.

papers.title: Zero-sum subsequences of cross number $1$ over cyclic groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, and let $\mathsf{T}(G)$ be the smallest integer $t$ such that every sequence of length $t$ over $G$ contains a nonempty zero-sum subsequence of cross number $1$. We determine the exact value of $\mathsf{T}(C_n)$ for every positive integer $n$, showing that $\mathsf{T}(C_n)=2n-1$ when $n$ is odd and $\mathsf{T}(C_n)=3n/2-1$ when $n$ is even. In particular, $\mathsf{T}(C_n)=\mathsf{s}(C_n)$ for odd $n$.

papers.title: Match Rate Is Not Match Quality
papers.abstract: Third-party identity-resolution vendors commonly emphasize match rate, the share of submitted records they can link to identifiers for advertising activation, as their core metric of quality. Yet a high match rate does not necessarily mean that those matched identifiers belong to the submitted records (i.e., the intended targets). In this paper we explore match quality as an alternative metric to match rate, utilizing a unique data set to evaluate match quality. We are able to compare two demographics, age and gender, from a submitted record (voter files) to the same demographics in self-reported surveys matched to mobile advertising identifiers linked together by two leading identity-resolution vendors. The data and matching was from 2019-20. There is substantial ambiguity in match quality of the returned records. First, both vendors' activation files contain multiple device identifiers per match. Second, match quality among audited pairs (Vendor A) and for explicitly labeled individual-level matches (Vendor B) is only 21.8% and 23.6%, respectively. Utilizing a mixture model that assumes that correct links always agree on these two demographics and incorrect links agree 10% of the time, these rates imply conditional identity-level precisions of approximately 15% and 13%, respectively. This paper utilizes identity-resolution products that are several years old, but the question we address remains fundamental: match rate alone cannot establish whether advertisers are reaching the people they intended. Evaluating identity resolution requires independent evidence of match quality alongside match rate.

papers.title: Pseudocompact MAD families under $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak c$
papers.abstract: We prove that if the bounding number $\mathfrak b$ equals the cardinality of the continuum $\mathfrak c$, then every infinite almost disjoint family of size less than $\mathfrak c$ can be extended to a maximal almost disjoint family whose Isbell--Mrówka space has a pseudocompact Vietoris hyperspace.

papers.title: Zippers and Twisters II: The lopsidedness of satellite systems around local massive galaxies emerges from a shifting cosmic web landscape
papers.abstract: We investigate the role of the cosmic web on the origin and strength of lopsidedness in the distributions of luminous dwarf satellites around massive galaxies analogs in the high-resolution hydrodynamic simulation NewHorizon. Using common lopsidedness estimators, we find that $>25\%$ of our sample display ``statistically significant" lopsidedness incompatible with expectations for dark matter sub-haloes. The NewHorizon sample is generally skewed towards being more lopsided than naive expectations. This cautions against using dark matter or under-resolved hydrodynamic simulations as a null-hypothesis to compare to real systems. We find broad, hemispheric lopsidedness to be much more prevalent than narrow lopsidedness inherited from group infall. Across all systems, the dividing plane between the richest and emptiest hemispheres is systematically aligned with a nearby intermediate-scale cosmic filament. Further analysis reveals that the lopsidedness of systems is largely inherited from that of the network of filaments feeding them. The most populated side almost systematically contains the highest number of filaments. Such anisotropies of local filament networks are often indicative of on-going or recent zippers (filament merger $<2$ Gyr). Converging filamentary structures therefore funnel satellites preferentially onto one side of host halos, naturally generating lopsided configurations without requiring galaxy mergers. Twister remnants (of high orbital momentum mergers of filaments) are also found on the richest hemisphere of our systems, perhaps reminiscent of vorticity preventing mergers hence causing satellites' pooling. These results suggest that lopsidedness is primarily an outcome of the evolution of the intermediate-scale cosmic web. This highlights the need for increased hydrodynamic resolution in simulations.

papers.title: Defining equations for two-block shallow ReLU pattern varieties
papers.abstract: We give a complete algebraic characterization of two-block shallow ReLU pattern varieties. We show that the determinantal equations arising from rank constraints imposed by the activation patterns generate the defining ideals, thereby proving a conjecture of Alexandr-Montúfar. The set-theoretic proof uses a characterization of orbit closures of matrix pencils in terms of the Kronecker canonical form.

papers.title: Implementation of LDA+Gutzwiller with Newton's method
papers.abstract: In order to calculate the electronic structure of correlated materials, we propose implementation of the LDA+Gutzwiller method with Newton's method. The self-consistence process, efficiency and convergence of calculation are improved dramatically by using Newton's method with golden section search and other improvement approaches. We compare the calculated results by applying the previous linear mix method and Newton's method. We have applied our code to study the electronic structure of several typical strong correlated materials, including SrVO$_3$, LaCoO$_3$, and La$_2$O$_3$Fe$_2$Se$_2$. Our results fit quite well with the previous studies.

papers.title: Materials representations organize transferable supervision for chemical extrapolation
papers.abstract: Materials discovery often requires chemical extrapolation beyond labeled data. When target compounds contain elements absent from training, which compounds of other elements provide transferable supervision remains unclear. Here we show that, without target-property labels, materials representations rank other elements by the supervision their compounds provide. Engineered descriptors rank them largely by elemental-property similarity, whereas a pretrained crystal-graph encoder ranks them by the geometry of its learned representation. At fixed training-set size, excluding the compounds of the encoder's six top-ranked elements raises formation-energy and bandgap errors by 100-110 meV per atom and 42-85 meV, versus little change for six lower-ranked elements. The rankings hold across properties, regressors and datasets. The encoder's ranking outperforms elemental-property similarity and periodic groups, suggesting that it captures how elements behave within compounds. Materials representations thus organize transferable supervision, which can be identified before model training, informing dataset assessment and label acquisition.

papers.title: Unpolarized Generalized Parton Distributions of the Nucleon in a Covariant Quark-Diquark Approach
papers.abstract: We study the unpolarized generalized parton distributions (GPDs) of the nucleon in a covariant quark-diquark approach, in which both scalar and axial-vector diquarks are treated as composite subsystems. Motivated by previous form factor studies, we introduce a vertex correction based on the pion cloud picture as a first exploratory treatment of pion cloud effects at the GPD level, in order to improve the description of $E^q(\xi, x, t)$ and related magnetic observables. At the model input scale, only valence quarks are included. With the vertex correction, the electromagnetic form factors $G_{E, M}$ and the mass form factor $A$ obtained from the Mellin moments of the GPDs agree well with those obtained from direct calculations. The vertex correction brings the evolved charge weighted distribution $\sum{e^q E^q(\xi, x, t)}$ closer to the phenomenological parametrization. The correction shifts transverse strength from the central region toward the peripheral region, consistent with the long range character of the pion cloud contribution. The transverse structure results further suggest a harder longitudinal momentum distribution in the central region of the nucleon than in its periphery. Furthermore, the evolved real part of the proton Compton form factor, $\mathrm{Re} \mathcal{H}(\xi, t)$, has a reasonable magnitude and follows the main trend of the Quantum Deep Neural Networks (QDNN) extraction. In addition, $\mathrm{Re} \mathcal{H}$ may be more sensitive to the ERBL region than the other physical quantities calculated in this work.

papers.title: Symplectic $\mathbb{CP}^n$ recognition and filling rigidity via Rabinowitz Floer homology
papers.abstract: We prove that a symplectic manifold $X$ admitting a pseudo-holomorphic line through two generic points, formulated as the non-vanishing of a genus zero Gromov--Witten invariant, is (rationally) homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb{CP}^n$, with identical first Chern class and quantum cohomology. Together with generalizations of this result to pseudo-holomorphic lines with tangency constraints, they provide a new mechanism for establishing the topological uniqueness of Liouville fillings of certain contact manifolds. We obtain filling rigidity for the ideal boundary of a class of affine varieties that admit $\mathbb{CP}^n$ as a compactification; notable examples include the ideal boundary of the complement of any hyperplane arrangement and $ST^*\mathbb{RP}^n$ for $n\ge 3$. The proofs are based on Rabinowitz Floer homology and its variants.

papers.title: Bernstein-Zelevinsky duality for equivariant vector bundles on Drinfeld spaces
papers.abstract: We study duality and finiteness of locally analytic representations arising from compactly supported coherent cohomology of Drinfeld spaces. We prove that Grothendieck--Serre duality for equivariant vector bundles realizes Bernstein--Zelevinsky duality of locally analytic representations. We follow the strategy of Fargues for $\ell$-adic sheaves and obtain resolutions of locally analytic representations by compactly induced representations. The resolutions motivate us to introduce the notion of locally analytic representations of compact presentation, which generalizes the notion of finitely presented representations. These representations are related to prim objects on the classifying stack in the sense of $6$-functor formalism and their extension groups to admissible locally analytic representations are finite-dimensional. As an application, we establish Serre duality for extension groups of locally analytic representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$ attached to non-trianguline de Rham Galois representations under the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence.

papers.title: Estimation-Aware Reachability
papers.abstract: Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability computes the states from which a system can be kept safe under worst-case disturbances, but it assumes the state is known exactly, whereas real robots act on noisy estimates whose uncertainty evolves with their motion. We extend Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability to the robot's belief, estimate and uncertainty, treating unexpected measurements as a bounded adversary and enlarging the unsafe set by the current uncertainty, so that certified states are safe with a prescribed probability. The formulation is compatible with existing solvers. In simulation, the resulting safety filters nearly eliminate the collisions of certaintyequivalent HJ and are less conservative than equally safe uncertainty-padding baselines. The implementation code is available at this https URL

papers.title: Near-optimal convergence of Widlund's method and numerical exploration of different implementations
papers.abstract: For linear systems arising from the discretization of certain classes of mathematical models, the splitting of the linear system into its Hermitian and skew-Hermitian parts has a physical meaning. If, in addition, the Hermitian part is positive definite, there exist Krylov subspace methods based on three-term recurrences where the Hermitian part is used as a preconditioner. Two such Krylov subspace methods are Widlund's method and Rapoport's method. In this paper we establish a ``near-optimal'' guarantee for the convergence of Widlund's method, showing that the overall convergence of Widlund's method is nearly as good as that of Rapoport's method. Specifically, we show that for every iteration $k$, there exists an iteration $j\leq k$ where the residual norm of Widlund's method is less than $\sqrt{k+1} $ times the residual norm of Rapoport's method at iteration $k$. This bound is sharp. We also provide a computational study on various implementations of Widlund's method in the exact and inexact cases, and show that certain implementations may stagnate while others do not, i.e., we look at the robustness of the different implementations. We recommend two implementations.

papers.title: Euler-Lagrange Equations Formulated in Terms of Angular Velocity
papers.abstract: We propose a novel variant of the Euler--Lagrange (EL) equation for rigid body rotation, explicitly formulated in terms of orientation parameters $\thh$ and angular velocity $\omm$. Variational analysis of the stationarity condition of the action integral for a Lagrangian in terms of $\thh$ and $\omm$ yields a modified EL formulation. For pure rotational motion, the proposed equation directly recovers equations of motion fully consistent with the classical Euler equations, bypassing explicit geometry-based torque analysis. Furthermore, the framework seamlessly accommodates coupled translational and rotational dynamics, as validated through a spring-suspended symmetrical top, exhibiting exact agreement with the Newton--Euler equations. We also identify an inherent discrepancy in the standard EL approach, demonstrating that applying a direct coordinate transformation $\dot\thh\mapsto\omm$ causes the resulting formulation to deviate from both the classical Euler equation and our proposed formulation. The proposed framework is expected to provide an intuitive, versatile modeling tool for spatial rigid body dynamics.

papers.title: Covering the Pauli Observables: Sampling Thresholds and the Design Effect of a Measurement Setting
papers.abstract: Quantum state tomography and shadow-based estimation rely on measuring Pauli observables. An experiment does not measure them one at a time: it chooses a measurement setting that assigns one of the bases X, Y or Z to each qubit, and a single run in that setting yields estimates of every Pauli observable compatible with it. We say that the setting covers those observables. We determine how many random settings cover a prescribed fraction of all Pauli observables. As the number of settings grows exponentially with the number of qubits, the covered fraction has a sharp threshold at a growth rate of $3^{3/4}$ per qubit, set by the rate-distortion function of covering at zero distortion. We give an explicit expression for the number of settings needed to reach a target fraction, accurate up to a remainder that reduces to a small oscillation for many qubits, and show that random sampling is asymptotically optimal up to a factor of less than 1.69. Coverage does not determine what a setting contributes to an estimator. Observables covered by one setting are estimated from the same outcomes, so their estimates are correlated. We quantify this correlation through the design effect of a setting, which equals the squared Pauli expectation that the setting captures and depends on the target state. We derive its mean over settings in closed form for every state and show that it can be estimated without bias from the measurement data. In simulations on six qubits, measuring settings needs 7.6 to 38 times fewer circuit runs than measuring the same number of observables independently. At high coverage, fitting the outcome histograms instead of averaged estimates roughly halves the reconstruction error, mainly because the fit counts how many settings cover each observable. The correlation itself costs such a fit about a factor of two, and a larger design effect signals more to gain from modeling it.

papers.title: Observation of Exact Mobility-Edge Phases in Two-Dimensional Photonic Quasicrystals
papers.abstract: Mobility edges, separating localized and extended states in energy, are central to localization physics. While exact mobility edges have been established in several one-dimensional quasiperiodic models, their realization in two dimensions remains largely unexplored. Here, we uncover a general route to exact mobility edges in the two-dimensional Aubry-Andre quasicrystal by introducing auxiliary subsystems. Through isospectral reduction, we reveal a hidden self-dual structure that yields exact mobility-edge conditions, separating extended, localized, and partially localized states in the spectrum. Tailoring the auxiliary structures controls the effective couplings and resulting mobility edge configurations, while auxiliary resonances further support flat-band states. In a decorated Lieb-type quasicrystal, we experimentally realize these predicted phases in photonic waveguide lattices and probe their energy-dependent localization through site-selective quench dynamics. Our results provide a versatile platform for controlling localization and can be readily extended to other physical platforms and higher-dimensional systems.

papers.title: Hurwitz equivalence in quandles of order at most four
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a quandle and let $m\geq 2$ be an integer. The $m$-braid group acts on the $m$-fold Cartesian power $X^m$ by the Hurwitz action. For an $m$-tuple $\boldsymbol{x}\in X^m$, we introduce two invariants of the Hurwitz action: the product $\Pi(\boldsymbol{x})$ of its entries in the associated group $\operatorname{As}(X)$ and the orbit multiplicities $\mu_w(\boldsymbol{x})$ $(w\in X)$. We prove that these two invariants completely classify Hurwitz equivalence classes for all quandles of order at most four. We also establish a complete classification of Hurwitz equivalence classes for a class of amalgamated sums of trivial quandles and a reduction theorem for disjoint sums with trivial quandles. Finally, we study the corresponding action of the virtual braid group. For this action, the orbit multiplicities alone give a complete classification for every quandle of order at most four.

papers.title: Chromatic heights of homotopy fixed points of iterated topological Hochschild homology of connective spectra
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be an $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-ring spectrum of height $m$. The chromatic redshift theorem implies that its $n$-fold iterated algebraic $K$-theory $K^{(n)}(R)$ has height $m+n$. Moreover, there is a natural map $K^{(n)}(R)\to (T^n\otimes R)^{hT^n}$, where $T^n\otimes R$ denotes the $n$-fold iterated topological Hochschild homology. Hence it is natural to ask whether the target also has height $m+n$. Although this fails in general, we prove that it holds whenever $R$ is connective and $m\geq1$. Our proof is based on an iterative calculation using Wilson spaces and relative topological Hochschild homology. As an application, we determine the support of the $T^n$-homotopy fixed points of $n$-fold iterated topological Hochschild homology of $\mathrm{BP}\langle m\rangle$ for $n=2,3$ with $\mathrm{BP}\langle m\rangle$ equipped with any $\mathbb{E}_3$-$\mathrm{MU}$-form.

papers.title: NEXONN: Advancing the NEXOTRANS Exoplanet Atmospheric Retrieval Framework with Transformer-Based Neural Posterior Estimation for JWST Transmission Spectroscopy of WASP-39b
papers.abstract: The James Webb Space Telescope is delivering unprecedented constraints on exoplanet atmospheres, but computationally intensive Bayesian retrievals challenge the transition from individual planets to population-level studies of planetary formation and evolution. We introduce NEXONN, a transformer-conditioned normalizing-flow framework within NEXOTRANS that enables rapid atmospheric posterior estimation with uncertainty quantification. Incorporating PandExo-based JWST noise, we benchmark NEXONN against PyMultiNest using simulated spectra and JWST observations of WASP-39 b (0.6-12 microns). For simulated MIRI/LRS data, eight posteriors achieve a mean overlap of 80.32%. Retrievals of combined NIRISS, NIRSpec, and MIRI observations yield consistent atmospheric properties. For the full dataset, NEXONN infers C/O = 0.82 (+0.01/-0.02) and [M/H] = 1.13 (+0.04/-0.04), compared with PyMultiNest values of 0.80 (+0.03/-0.01) and 1.19 (+0.05/-0.03). Divergence metrics, Wasserstein distances, posterior overlaps, and coverage tests assess posterior fidelity and uncertainty calibration, revealing parameter-dependent differences. Once trained, NEXONN performs posterior inference within seconds, enabling scalable population studies of exoplanet atmospheric composition, formation, and evolution.

papers.title: From Powers--Stormer to Loewner Inertia: Weighted Trace Functionals and Orthogonal Perturbations
papers.abstract: We study the weighted trace functional $\TT_{f,h}(A,B)=\Tr h^\circ(A-B)[f(A)-f(B)]$, where $h^\circ(H)=h(H_+)-h(H_-)$. The Jordan decomposition of $A-B$ yields exact common-roof decompositions for operator monotone and operator convex functions, including the Powers--Størmer and Ricard trace comparisons. The orthogonal cross term gives a finite rank-one realization of the classical conditional Löwner-matrix criterion for operator convexity. For powers, resolvent squares yield a coupling-dependent Mellin strip, endpoint identities, and quantitative bounds on off-sector spectral interactions. Linearization produces positive and inverse moment subspaces of power Löwner matrices. A confluent determinant calculation provides the remaining sign data in the known inertia classification. We give explicit equality conditions and a finite-copy application of the Powers--Størmer equality case.

papers.title: Fixed and periodic points of bi-dual intersection operators
papers.abstract: We classify the fixed and periodic points, up to positive dilation, of the operators $\mathbb I_m=\mathbb I_{m,m+1}$ in the indexed bi-dual intersection family associated with centro-section integrals. For $n\ge3$ and $1\le m\le n-2$, a star body satisfies $\mathbb I_m^{\,r}K=cK$ for some $c>0$ and an integer $r\ge1$ if and only if it is an origin-centered Euclidean ball. No convexity, origin symmetry, or initial differentiability is assumed. An exact Grassmannian graph representation gives a decreasing weight and yields a strictly positive linear increment under continuous Steiner symmetrization unless the body is already symmetric. At a fixed point, a uniform radial Taylor estimate makes the same volume-preserving increment quadratic. Sobolev estimates for the spherical Radon transform and its adjoint supply the required regularity. Independently, a strict Lyapunov inequality reduces every periodic point up to dilation to a fixed point. We also prove automatic positivity and smoothness for bounded nonnegative solutions and local geometric convergence of normalized iterates near the ball.

papers.title: Stationary Quantum Time Series: Spectral Theory of Process Memory and Measurement Records
papers.abstract: Classical time series analysis converts temporal dependence into structure that can be learned from a single observed trajectory, through stationarity, ergodicity, spectral representation, and finite-memory models. Quantum experiments are naturally time series: every run is a sequence of interventions and outcomes, and the memory of an open system is written in its temporal statistics. However, the classical foundation cannot be translated directly: measuring a process and forgetting the outcome differs from not measuring at all, so no single family of joint probability distributions describes a quantum process. We develop a process-tensor framework for stationary quantum time series and establish its first structural theorems. For stationary combs of finite quantum Markov order l relative to a fixed informationally complete causal break, we construct a finite-dimensional causal transfer map of dimension at most d^{4l}, where d bounds the system Hilbert-space dimension at each step. ... These results supply the stationary foundation on which quantum spectral analysis, model identification, and single-trajectory inference can be built.

papers.title: Breaking the Myth of Four-Tier Stacked Transistors for Logic: an Investigation from Process to Device and Block-Level PPA
papers.abstract: For the first time, this work evaluated whether 4-tier stacked transistors can translate the straightforward density gains into realistic chip-level scaling benefits. A practical dual-sided 4-tier transistor-stacking CFFET (Flipped CFET-to-CFET) process was proposed, on which a DTCO framework spanning standard-cell design, local interconnects, RO analysis, and physical implementation was built under 2A node design rules. The CFFET was also benchmarked with its 2-tier transistor-stacking counterparts FFET. Among CFFET configurations, the best-performing Symmetric Power still lags FFET by 11.2% in RO frequency due to the complex MOL parasitics. At the block level, CFFET reduces the Ibex RISC-V core area by only 12.8% (far below the 40% nominal cell-height reduction), while running 10.9% slower at iso-power. We further introduced a novel Tetris-like cell stitching to minimize the area overhead, which allows non-rectangular cell design and recovers 7.4% area in a 1-bit ALU design. An optimized NanoStack CFFET was finally proposed, inspired by previous work. This work indicates that straightforward vertical 4-tier stacking proves insufficient to guarantee enough PPA benefits, though the resulting design insights may guide future advanced architectures.

papers.title: Hydrodynamic limit of the Toda lattice
papers.abstract: In this paper we consider the Toda lattice under random, spatially inhomogeneous initial data, meaning that its initial momenta and interparticle spacings are independent and their laws may slowly vary in space. When the density is strictly positive (but sufficiently small), we identify the model's hydrodynamic limit under Euler scaling. More precisely, we prove that spatial averages of each of the model's local conserved quantities converge to moments of a density $m_{\tau}(\lambda,q)$ solving the generalized hydrodynamic equation predicted by Doyon arXiv:1902.07624 and Spohn arXiv:1902.07751 . To do so, we justify the notion that the Toda lattice can be thought of as a dense collection of many "quasiparticles" that interact through scattering. As in Aggarwal arXiv:2503.08018 , we define these quasiparticles through spectral properties of the Toda Lax matrix, but in our inhomogeneous setting we must now show that the eigenvectors of this Lax matrix remain localized throughout the dynamics. The core of our work is to show that, with high probability, the quasiparticle trajectories converge to the characteristic curves of the generalized hydrodynamic equation.

papers.title: SFiD: Self-Supervised Fitness-Driven Optimization for Next-Generation Networking
papers.abstract: Next-generation (NG) wireless networks face increasingly complex and dynamic optimization challenges driven by data-intensive applications and massive device connectivity. Existing methods suffer from one or more limitations, including high computational complexity, poor scalability and adaptability, reliance on large labeled datasets, or weak generalization in dynamic and non-convex wireless environments. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a self-supervised fitness-driven diffusion (SFiD) method that autonomously generates its own training data and iteratively learns from it. It also exhibits strong generalization capabilities and the ability to effectively tackle challenging optimization problems. We validate the convergence of our proposed method to the global optimum on both analytical convex and non-convex optimization problems. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, we consider reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) phaseshift optimization in cell-free massive multiple-input multipleoutput (CF-mMIMO) systems with imperfect channel state information and spatial correlation at the RIS as a case study. Specifically, we develop SFiD-C for continuous variable optimization and apply it to optimize continuous RIS phase shifts in CF-mMIMO systems. We also develop SFiD-D for discrete variable optimization and apply it to optimize discrete RIS phase shifts in CF-mMIMO systems. Furthermore, we develop a binary neural network (BNN) based version of SFiDD for reducing its computational complexity, referred to as SFiD-D (BNN). Finally, our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed methods markedly improve computational efficiency and achieve comparable or superior performance compared to meta-heuristic and DRL benchmarks for both continuous and discrete RIS phase-shift optimization.

papers.title: Improved Leverage Score Sampling for Constrained Active Linear Regression
papers.abstract: In this paper we study active learning for constrained linear regression. Given a design matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$, a constraint set $C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$, and query access to $b\in\mathbb{R}^n$, we seek an approximate solution to $\min_{x\in C}\|Ax-b\|_2^2$ using as few queries as possible. This problem arises in many scientific and engineering applications, and randomized leverage score sampling provides a powerful method to solve it. However, existing leverage score methods ignore the constraint or encode it through ridge regularization, suffering unfavorable query complexity for anisotropic constraint sets. We propose ellipsoid-regularized leverage scores, where we approximate the constraint set by an outer ellipsoid and use its shape matrix to bias sampling toward directions that matter under the constraint geometry. We prove that the query complexity is governed by an anisotropic effective dimension $d_{\text{eff}}(C)\le d$. With appropriate parameters, $O(d_{\text{eff}}(C)\log d/\varepsilon^2)$ queries suffice to return a point in $C$ with objective value at most $(1+\varepsilon)$ times the optimum. This bound can substantially improve on the standard leverage-score bound, since anisotropic constraints can make $d_{\text{eff}}(C)$ much smaller than $d$. For convex constraints, we improve the dependence on $\varepsilon$ from $1/\varepsilon^2$ to $1/\varepsilon$. We also prove two lower bounds: first, the $d/\varepsilon^2$ dependence is unavoidable without convexity assumptions on $C$, and second, in some regimes, the effective dimension dependence $d_{\mathrm{eff}}(C)/\varepsilon$ is necessary for ellipsoidal constraints. Experiments on synthetic regression problems and a parametric heat conduction problem show lower regression error than standard baselines for similar query budget.

papers.title: On pluriclosed torsion-critical Hermitian metrics
papers.abstract: In our previous work, we studied the squared $L^2$-norm functionals $\mathcal G$ of Gauduchon's torsion $1$-form and $\mathcal F$ of the Chern torsion over the space of all Hermitian metrics with unit volume on a compact complex manifold. We introduced torsion-critical metrics as critical points of $\mathcal F$. In this paper, We prove that a pluriclosed and astheno-Kähler metric is torsion-critical if and only if it is Kähler. In particular, every compact pluriclosed torsion-critical Hermitian threefold is Kähler. We also give explicit examples and derive geometric consequences under additional curvature assumptions.

papers.title: Character codegrees in $π$-separable groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the set $\operatorname{C}_{\pi}(G)$ of irreducible characters of a finite $\pi$-separable group $G$ whose codegrees (defined by Qian as $\operatorname{cod}(\chi)=|G:\ker\chi|/\chi(1)$) are $\pi$-numbers, in relation to the Isaacs--Gajendragadkar classes of $\pi$-special characters $\operatorname{X}_{\pi}(G)$ and $\operatorname{B}_{\pi}$-characters $\operatorname{B}_{\pi}(G)$.

papers.title: Developing a Subdistrict-Level Economic Progress Index Using Geospatial Data
papers.abstract: This paper develops an Economic Progress Index (EPI), a composite measure built from Earth Observation (EO) and open geospatial data with unsupervised Principal Component Analysis (PCA) weighting. The index captures the observable productive and enabling capacity of local economies and the intensity with which economic space is used. Sub-national monitoring in developing economies is held back by sparse data: district GDP estimates arrive with multi-year lags, rely on price deflators and top-down allocation, and do not exist at the subdistrict (taluka/tehsil) scale where place-based policy is targeted. The EPI fuses multi-sensor satellite data, gridded population and OpenStreetMap road and amenity networks across 357 subdistricts of Maharashtra, India, over 46 quarters (2015 Q1 - 2026 Q2). Seasonal-Trend decomposition using LOESS (STL) separates long-run trends from monsoon and crop-cycle seasonality. A non-negative PCA gives sign-consistent, interpretable weights and rankings nearly identical to standard PCA ($\rho$ = 0.998). Across districts, the index explains 74% of the variation in the NFHS-5 wealth index, 52% in household consumption (HCES 2023-24) and about 78% in real district GDP levels (65% in logs), but does not track short-run output growth. Because it measures structural capacity rather than annual output, the index kept rising through the FY2020-21 COVID-19 contraction. Across Maharashtra's six revenue divisions, relative inequality fell by 44% even as the absolute gap between leading and lagging divisions widened by 32%; district-level $\beta$-convergence implies a half-life of about 14 years. The framework offers a scalable, deflator-free basis for structural monitoring in data-sparse economies.

papers.title: Sharp orthonormal Strichartz estimates for the Schrödinger equation in all remaining cases
papers.abstract: We study orthonormal Strichartz estimates for the free Schrödinger equation in homogeneous Sobolev spaces $\dot H^s$. We resolve the remaining open cases concerning the optimal summability of the coefficients. Together with earlier results and counterexamples, our theorems complete the classification for nonnegative Sobolev regularity $0\le s<d/2$.

papers.title: Critical--localized reentry under periodic spacer control
papers.abstract: Tracking a fixed fraction of a quasiperiodic spectrum tests whether repeated critical--localized alternation extends over a nonzero spectral weight. We find such alternation in a matched-dimer chain by varying only the spacer on-site energies and following a fixed interval of integrated-density-of-states (IDS) labels. An exact Bloch-determinant identity links the physical transfer discriminant to the bands of a periodic reference operator. For the golden cell frequency, we prove that, on a common full-measure set of phases and for every finite value of the spacer control, the physical spectrum in the open reference bands is critical, with purely singular-continuous spectrum and zero Lyapunov exponent, while the spectrum strictly outside the bands is pure point, with exponentially decaying eigenfunctions. Validated IDS bounds certify repeated critical--localized alternation of the same fixed spectral fraction at successive spacer controls. Spacer shifts move the physical levels and reference-band edges at different rates, allowing us to reshape finite-chain return windows and place their endpoints at prescribed controls. An affine recalibration relocates the control family exactly.

papers.title: A Dual-SOM Learner Model of Instructional Efficiency within Cognitive Load Theory
papers.abstract: This paper presents a novel methodological framework, integrating a dual self-organising map (SOM) neural network architecture with Cognitive Load Theory (CLT), for assessing instructional efficiency within learning environments. By representing curriculum content as a directed acyclic graph of topic dependencies, the proposed model captures collective learning behaviour across two core dimensions: academic performance and subjective/introspective mental effort. During SOM training, representative data sets of successful learner trajectories are compressed into two topologically ordered, identically structured neural networks: PSOM (performance space) and ESOM (mental effort space). By pairing these behavioural maps, the model serves as a decision-support tool that enables instructors to simultaneously pinpoint structural instructional design defects, such as hidden topic prerequisites, and evaluate collective cognitive load profiles. The implementation and performance of the PSOM component (and, by extension, its symmetrical twin, ESOM) is linked to an earlier modelling study employing a SOM with identical structure and encoding semantics situated in the same domain (i.e., a learning environment). This paper combines the study of behavioural phenomena with theoretical work on human cognitive architecture via SOM neurocomputational cognitive behavioural modelling.

papers.title: Benchmarking Traditional and Learning-Based Reference-Free Compressors for Long-Read Sequencing Data
papers.abstract: Long-read sequencing technologies generate large volumes of data, creating substantial storage and transmission demands. Although reference-based compressors can achieve high compression, their reliance on an appropriate reference genome limits their use. We present LRCBench, a benchmark and survey of reference-free lossless compressors for long-read sequencing data. We review traditional and learning-based general-purpose and sequencing-specific methods, then evaluate 35 compressors on 16 real-world datasets from Oxford Nanopore and PacBio platforms. We compare compression ratio, storage savings, runtime, peak memory use, and robustness across datasets. Learning-based compressors are evaluated on six MinION datasets because of their high computational costs. CoLoRd achieves the best overall compression ratios in our experiments, while other methods offer trade-offs in speed, memory use, and robustness. We also examine multithreaded speedup and discuss future directions in parallel acceleration, privacy protection, adaptive parameter tuning, and hardware-algorithm co-design.

papers.title: A State-Level Assessment of Space Weather Impact on the Virginia Power Grid: From Vulnerability to Mitigation Strategies
papers.abstract: Contemporary methodologies exist for assessing the nationwide impacts of geomagnetically induced currents (GICs), such as the Coupled Space Weather Impact Model (C-SWIM), which links power grid vulnerability with economic losses. Yet regional mitigation requires adapting the national model to the local transmission network so operators and planners can identify substations at risk and evaluate economic and population consequences and protective actions. We present the first adaptation of C-SWIM to Virginia, modeling the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnection, which includes Dominion Energy Virginia and Appalachian Power. Its extra high voltage network was assessed under the May 2024 Gannon, October 2003 Halloween, and March 2015 St. Patrick's Day storms in addition to nine return period scenarios derived from statistical fits to 92 historical events. Using the Leontief consumption and production input-output model, we estimated daily losses of USD 145.5M for a 100-year storm and USD 230.6M for a 250-year storm, with 339,000-535,000 people and up to 12,000 businesses at risk of power outage. The Ghosh input-output model was used to evaluate three island selection algorithms for protective islanding, which temporarily disconnects parts of the grid to reduce transformer damage. Only one algorithm yielded benefits exceeding costs across all twelve scenarios, with avoided losses up to USD 9.69M per day and a cost of USD 0.204M per intervention. However, these islanding benefits assume disconnection for 6 hours and transformer replacement after 365 days. Moreover, the analysis uses national economic relationships and models only transformer thermal failure, excluding voltage collapse, cascading failures, and restoration. Transmission operators and state energy policymakers can use this statewide assessment to prioritize regional monitoring and appraise protective islanding.

papers.title: Finite-time stochastic resetting in bounded domains: competing targets, energetic cost, and optimal search strategies
papers.abstract: We investigate the first-passage dynamics and energetic cost of a Brownian particle subject to finite-time stochastic resetting in a bounded one-dimensional domain with two absorbing boundaries. Unlike conventional instantaneous resetting, the particle is returned to a prescribed resetting position through a finite-duration process driven by a linear trapping potential. By solving the corresponding backward equations, we derive analytical expressions for the mean global first-passage time and the splitting probabilities. Our results show that the finite duration of the return process can substantially modify the dependence of the mean global first-passage time on the resetting rate. In particular, we identify a critical trapping strength above which resetting can accelerate the search process, and characterize how the range of favorable resetting positions depends on the trapping strength. We further characterize the energetic cost of resetting by deriving the generating function of the total work and obtaining an analytical expression for its mean value. For the linear trapping potential considered here, we establish an exact relation between the mean total work and the mean cumulative return time. This relation allows us to establish a quantitative trade-off between the mean global first-passage time and the energetic expenditure, revealing how the finite duration of the return process affects search efficiency. Brownian dynamics simulations confirm our theoretical predictions.

papers.title: Spectral Engineering of Charge Localization and Work Reliability in Collective Quantum Batteries
papers.abstract: The performance of a quantum battery depends not only on how much energy it stores, but also on how rapidly useful charge can be restored after work extraction. We show how engineering the reservoir spectrum connects these properties in an interacting collective-spin battery. Interactions separate the Dicke transition frequencies, allowing frequency-selective pumping and loss to control where excitation accumulates and how populations move along the ladder. Analytical results relate the pump-to-loss ratio to charge localization, fluctuations, and extractable work. Two reservoirs producing the same mean charge can nevertheless exhibit markedly different localization and charging times. Under repeated extraction, finite-time recharging also generates correlations between successive work outputs. At matched mean work, these correlations can reverse the ordering of single-cycle and long-time fluctuations: a protocol with larger fluctuations in individual strokes can deliver more reliable accumulated work. An exact counting relation connects these statistics to net charging-energy transfer, while relaxation modes distinguish recovery of the stationary state from recovery of useful work. Finally, local dephasing redistributes population among collective-spin sectors, leading to an exact stationary symmetry-dilution law and a finite operating window for work extraction under a collective transverse controller.

papers.title: Geometry-bridge flow matching for blind rigid-motion correction in head cone-beam CT
